topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Does Ohio maintain a separate "principal broker" license or a separate principal-broker examination, distinct from an ordinary real estate broker's license?
choice_a: Yes -- a candidate must pass a distinct principal-broker exam after already holding a broker's license
choice_b: Yes -- principal brokers are licensed under a different statutory chapter with different age and education minimums
choice_c: No -- principal broker is a designation held by one of a brokerage's already-licensed brokers, not a separate license class or exam
choice_d: No -- but principal brokers must additionally be licensed as attorneys
explanation: ORC 4735.081 requires every brokerage to designate one of its licensed brokers as its "principal broker." That person qualifies through the same broker examination and licensure path under ORC 4735.07-.08 as any other broker; Ohio does not create a separate principal-broker license tier or exam.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Every Ohio brokerage must designate at least one of its licensed brokers to serve in what role under ORC 4735.081?
explanation: ORC 4735.081 ("Designation of principal broker") requires every brokerage to designate at least one of its licensed brokers as the brokerage's principal broker, who then bears the statutory oversight duties described in the same section.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A licensed broker at ABC Realty has held a broker's license for 15 years but has never been designated principal broker of any brokerage. Compared to a newly licensed broker who IS designated principal broker on day one, did the newly designated principal broker take a different, more advanced broker exam?
choice_a: No -- both individuals took the identical broker examination; the principal-broker role is a designation assigned after licensure, not an exam-based distinction
choice_b: Yes -- the newly designated principal broker had to pass an additional supervisory exam module
choice_c: Yes -- only candidates for principal broker are exempt from the standard broker exam
choice_d: No -- but the principal broker must hold a higher pre-license education credit total under ORC 4735.07
explanation: This is the recurring Ohio-specific distinction: principal broker status is assigned under ORC 4735.081 to a broker who already holds the standard license under ORC 4735.07-.08. There is no separate, more advanced exam or license tier tied to the designation itself.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), which of the following is an explicit duty of a principal broker?
choice_a: Personally negotiate every purchase agreement the brokerage enters into
choice_b: Oversee and direct the operations of the brokerage
choice_c: Serve as the brokerage's registered agent for service of process
choice_d: Personally appraise every listed property before sale
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(1) lists overseeing and directing the operations of the brokerage as a principal broker's first enumerated duty -- the umbrella responsibility under which the section's more specific duties fall.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), a principal broker must ensure that which required notice is displayed in the brokerage's offices?
choice_b: A list of all pending litigation against the brokerage
choice_d: The principal broker's personal home address
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(3) makes displaying the fair housing statement in the brokerage's offices (and on required pamphlets) an explicit principal-broker duty.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), what must a principal broker do regarding license renewals and terminated affiliated licensees?
choice_a: Nothing -- license renewal is handled exclusively by the Ohio Division of Real Estate without broker involvement
choice_b: Delegate all renewal and termination handling to the terminated licensee personally
choice_c: Renew licenses only for salespersons who close 10 or more transactions per year
choice_d: Handle renewal of brokerage/branch licenses and pay applicable fees, and return the licenses of terminated salespersons and brokers
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(4)-(6) makes the principal broker responsible for renewing the brokerage's and branch offices' licenses and paying applicable fees, maintaining the licenses of the brokerage and its affiliated licensees, and returning the licenses of salespersons or brokers who are terminated.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), what must a principal broker do with respect to the brokerage's trust and special bank accounts?
choice_a: Comply with trust/special account requirements and maintain complete, accurate trust and transaction account records
choice_b: Nothing -- trust account compliance is solely a licensee-by-licensee obligation with no principal-broker role
choice_c: Close all trust accounts and route escrow funds directly to the title company instead
choice_d: Delegate trust account compliance entirely to the bank holding the account
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(7)-(8) makes a principal broker responsible for complying with the brokerage's trust and special bank account requirements and for maintaining complete and accurate trust and transaction account records.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), what must a principal broker develop regarding agency relationships?
choice_b: A written company policy on agency relationships
choice_c: Nothing -- agency policy is governed exclusively by each individual salesperson's own practice
choice_d: A policy that applies only to buyer clients, not seller clients
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(9) requires the principal broker to develop and maintain a written company policy addressing agency relationships, giving affiliated licensees a documented standard to follow.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), what must a principal broker ensure regarding payment of affiliated salespersons?
choice_a: That salespersons are paid only in the form of an annual bonus
choice_b: That commission payments to salespersons are optional at the principal broker's discretion
choice_c: That affiliated licensees are paid as required by statute
choice_d: That salespersons are paid directly by the buyer or seller, not the brokerage
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(11) makes it a principal-broker duty to pay affiliated licensees as required by statute, tying into the separate prohibition in ORC 4735.18(A)(31) against failing to promptly pay a salesperson's earned commission share.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), what practice must a principal broker establish regarding who performs licensed real estate activities on the brokerage's behalf?
choice_a: A practice permitting any brokerage employee, licensed or not, to show property to the public
choice_b: A practice delegating all licensed activity exclusively to unlicensed administrative staff
choice_c: There is no such requirement -- staffing decisions are entirely unregulated
choice_d: A practice ensuring that only affiliated licensees perform licensed activities for the brokerage
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(12) requires the principal broker to establish practices that ensure only affiliated LICENSEES perform licensed real estate activities, reinforcing the general prohibition on unauthorized/unlicensed practice found elsewhere in Chapter 4735.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), what oversight role does a principal broker have regarding brokerage advertising?
choice_a: Overseeing the brokerage's compliance with advertising requirements
choice_b: None -- individual licensees bear sole responsibility for their own advertisements
choice_c: Approving advertising budgets only, with no compliance role
choice_d: Overseeing advertising only for listings the principal broker personally holds
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(13) makes overseeing the brokerage's compliance with advertising requirements (such as those in ORC 4735.16) an explicit principal-broker duty.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(C), what general supervisory duty does a principal broker owe with respect to affiliated licensees' licensed activity?
choice_a: No supervisory duty -- each affiliated licensee is independently responsible with no brokerage-level oversight
choice_b: General oversight of the licensed activity conducted by affiliated licensees
choice_c: Oversight limited strictly to new licensees in their first year
choice_d: Oversight only during formal Commission audits
explanation: ORC 4735.081(C)(14) closes the enumerated duty list with a catch-all: the principal broker must generally oversee the licensed activity of the brokerage's affiliated licensees.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(D), may a principal broker assign supervisory duties to a management-level licensee?
choice_a: No -- ORC 4735.081 duties are non-delegable under any circumstances
choice_b: Yes, but only to another principal broker at a different brokerage
choice_c: Yes -- the principal broker may assign these duties to a management level licensee under OAC 1301:5-6-01
choice_d: Yes, but only with prior written approval from every affiliated licensee
explanation: ORC 4735.081(D) permits a principal broker to assign the section's duties to a qualifying management level licensee as defined in OAC 1301:5-6-01.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: If a principal broker delegates supervisory duties to a qualified management level licensee under OAC 1301:5-6-01, is the principal broker relieved of ultimate responsibility for those duties?
choice_a: Yes -- delegation fully transfers all legal responsibility to the management level licensee
choice_b: Yes, but only for trust account duties specifically
choice_c: No relief question arises because delegation under OAC 1301:5-6-01 is not permitted in Ohio
choice_d: No -- the assignment of supervisory duties does not relieve the principal broker of responsibility to actively oversee and direct the brokerage's operations
explanation: OAC 1301:5-6-01 states directly that the assignment of supervisory duties to management level licensees does not relieve the principal broker from the principal broker's responsibility to actively oversee and direct the operations of the business conducted on behalf of the brokerage. Delegation spreads the workload, not the ultimate accountability.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under OAC 1301:5-6-01, what two conditions must be true of a licensee for that licensee to qualify as a "management level licensee"?
choice_a: The licensee has been assigned oversight of a main office, branch office, or division, AND those duties include supervising affiliated licensees whose agency duties to clients may conflict with other affiliated licensees
choice_b: The licensee has at least 10 years of experience AND has personally closed 100 transactions
choice_c: The licensee holds a broker's license AND is the brokerage's sole shareholder
choice_d: The licensee has completed 240 hours of pre-license education AND passed the broker exam with a perfect score
explanation: OAC 1301:5-6-01 defines a management level licensee by two conjunctive criteria: (1) assigned management duties involving oversight of the brokerage's main office, a branch office, or a division, and (2) those duties include supervising affiliated licensees whose agency duties to their clients may conflict with those of other affiliated licensees.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: Under ORC 4735.081(E), may a single broker serve as principal broker for more than one brokerage at the same time?
choice_a: No -- Ohio law limits any individual to serving as principal broker of a single brokerage
choice_b: Yes -- the superintendent may permit a broker to be licensed with and act as principal broker for more than one brokerage
choice_c: Yes, but only if the two brokerages share the identical office address
choice_d: No -- multiple-brokerage principal broker arrangements were eliminated by the 2001 education reforms
explanation: ORC 4735.081(E) allows the superintendent to permit a broker to be licensed with, and act as principal broker for, more than one brokerage -- a multiple-brokerage principal-broker arrangement subject to superintendent approval.

topic: Broker Supervision, Principal Brokers & Management-Level Licensees
question: A principal broker delegates day-to-day supervision of a branch office's trust account recordkeeping to a qualified management level licensee. Six months later, a Commission audit finds the branch's trust account records are incomplete. Who bears principal responsibility for that violation?
choice_a: The management level licensee exclusively, since supervisory duties were formally assigned to them
choice_b: Neither party, because the recordkeeping duty became the bank's responsibility once delegated
choice_c: The principal broker, because delegation to a management level licensee does not relieve the principal broker of ultimate responsibility to oversee the brokerage's operations
choice_d: The affiliated salespersons at the branch office, since they generated the underlying transactions
explanation: Consistent with OAC 1301:5-6-01's explicit language, assigning supervisory or recordkeeping duties to a management level licensee spreads the day-to-day workload but does not shift ultimate statutory responsibility away from the principal broker.
